_comment: Tool definitions for the Anthropic Messages API, one per groma-api route. Paste the `tools` array into client.messages.create(tools=...). Each tool maps to a GET on the base URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8787) and your executor only has to build the URL and return the JSON body verbatim. `strict: true` guarantees the arguments validate against the schema.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List the Revit models available to query. Returns their ids, which every other tool takes as `model`. Call this first when you do not already know the model id.

tools.name: model_summary
tools.description: Overview of one Revit model: how many elements it holds, how many are model elements (real building elements rather than annotation or type definitions), how many carry geometry, how many rooms and storeys, and the most frequent Revit classes and categories. `model_elements_without_level` is how many model elements sit on no storey at all, so per-storey counts sum to less than `model_elements` by exactly that much - say so rather than presenting the storey counts as the whole model. Call this before querying elements so you know which class and category values exist in this model.

tools.name: query_elements
tools.description: Search the elements of one Revit model. All filters combine with AND and any may be omitted. Returns a page of elements plus `total`, the number of matches, which is usually larger than the page - use `total` to answer counting questions such as 'how many doors are on Level 2' rather than counting the returned page. Numeric parameter values are in Revit's internal units (feet, square feet, radians) unless the parameter also carries `storage_value` with a `unit_name`; when it does, quote that converted value, and when it does not, do not present the raw number as metres or millimetres.

class.description: Exact Revit class, case-insensitive. Common values: SWall (walls), Floor, FamilyInstance (doors, windows, columns, railings and other placed families), RoomElem, Level, StairsRun. Use model_summary to see what this model has.

category.description: Exact Revit category, case-insensitive, e.g. OST_Walls, OST_Doors, OST_Windows. Note that real placed instances usually carry NO category of their own - it lives on their type - so filter instances by `class` and use `category` mainly for type definitions.

storey.description: Storey `id` from list_levels. This is the exact way to name a storey: it matches every Level record folded into that storey, which a level name cannot do when list_levels marks the name `ambiguous_name` (the same name at two elevations). Prefer this over `level`.

level.description: Storey name as returned by list_levels, e.g. '02 Этаж'. Names are not unique - where list_levels reports `ambiguous_name` for a name, this filter merges the storeys sharing it and the count covers both. Use `storey` when you mean one storey.

name.description: Substring of the element's own name.

q.description: Free-text substring searched across name, class, category, level, type, family and every text parameter. Use this when you do not know which field holds the term.

model_elements.description: Keep only real building elements of the model, excluding type definitions, annotation and view artefacts. Set this true for a question about the built fabric - walls, floors, stairs, roofs, placed families. Do NOT set it when asking about rooms or levels: they are not building elements and the flag drops them, so `class=RoomElem` with this flag returns 0 on a model full of rooms. When the flag removed matches the answer says so in `excluded_as_not_model_elements`; a 0 total alongside a non-zero one there means the flag, not the model.

with_geometry.description: Keep only elements whose geometry was recovered.

offset.description: Elements to skip, for paging. Default 0.

tools.name: get_element
tools.description: Fetch one element of a Revit model by its Revit element id, with every recovered field: class, category, the storey it is on, its type and family, all parameters, geometry if any, and `source`, which locates the record inside the .rvt file.

id.description: Revit element id, as returned in the `id` field by query_elements.

tools.name: list_rooms
tools.description: Every room in a Revit model, with the storey it sits on and its full parameter set - room number, name, purpose, areas and any project-specific schedule parameters. Room parameters are usually project parameters, so their numeric values do carry a converted `storage_value` and `unit_name` (for example square metres). Use this for questions about rooms, apartments, areas or what a space is for.

tools.name: list_levels
tools.description: The storeys of a Revit model, lowest first, with their elevation in metres, how many model elements and rooms stand on each, and `ambiguous_name` where another storey carries the same name at a different elevation. A storey here is a level model elements actually stand on, with every Level record describing the same place folded together - `level_ids` lists them, and one storey is commonly a dozen records. Pass a storey's `id` as the `storey` filter of query_elements; that reaches all of its records. The per-storey counts here already answer 'how many elements are on each floor' without further queries.
